pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Thallium Toxicity THE SMOKING GUN: Rapidly progressive painful distal sensory neuropathy followed by delayed massive alopecia and transverse nail bands (Mees' lines) PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Thallium mimics potassium ions due to their similar ionic radii, disrupting the Na+/K+-ATPase pump and cellular respiration. It also avidly binds to intracellular sulfhydryl groups in enzymes and structural proteins. This leads to widespread mitochondrial dysfunction, manifesting initially as agonizing peripheral nerve damage, autonomic dysregulation, and gastrointestinal distress, followed weeks later by the disruption of keratin cross-linking which causes dramatic hair loss.
